Q: Can the hasNext() iterator method return false first and then true? A:

The Answers by rzwitserloot and by Jon Skeet are correct and smart. Here's an alternative approach for you to consider, as mentioned in the Comments.

Queue

You said in this Comment:

I want the user to control the data retrieval process (a pull model for this method).

That is precisely the purpose of a Queue, an interface built into Java. “A collection designed for holding elements prior to processing.” per the Javadoc — just as the name “queue” suggests.

Think of a Queue as a pipeline. On one end, a producer drops things into the pipeline. The things slide over to the other end of the pipeline. On the other end, a consumer pulls things out of the pipeline.

Rather than try to implement an java.util.Iterator, just use an implementation of Queue. Establish a producer and a consumer, both tied to the same Queue instance.

  • Use one thread to retrieve data from your external system over time. Each time data is received, post it as an element in the queue.
  • Another thread consumes elements from the queue. Each element is then processed per your business logic.

BlockingQueue

If you want that consumer thread to wait for the queue to become non-empty when retrieving an element, use a BlockingQueue. Know that BlockingQueue implementations are thread-safe. A BlockingQueue may be capacity bounded, if you wish, rejecting added elements while the limit is reached.

See example code on the BlockingQueue Javadoc.

Q: Encrypt Web.Config (Web.Release.config) Transform files using aspnet_regiis A:

After a lot of digging around, I found a way to use aspnet_regiis to encrypt the different environment Web.config transform files without having to actually deploy them and then encrypt them on server after the fact. You can use msbuild to run the transform while specifying an environment to target (Release for example) locally:

msbuild /t:TransformWebConfig /p:Configuration=Release

The transformed Web.config file will now be in your project directory: obj/Release/TransformWebConfig/transformed/. (Again, using Release in this example.)

You can then run aspnet_regiis to encrypt the Web.config section you wish to encrypt in that directory.

After you have encrypted the section, copy it over to your Web.Release.config file in your solution. Be sure to include the attribute xtd:Transform="Replace" in the config section you are copying over.

You can repeat those steps for any other environments you may have (Staging for example).

This assumes you are sharing your IIS encryption key across environments. If you are using unique keys for each environment, then you would need to encrypt each environment Web.config file with the key used on that server.
